title: Dangermond Preserve — Creek Water Outlines (m3-v2, channel ribbon on the raw lidar bed, for m3-v2, m4-v1 and m5-v1)
snippet: One continuous ribbon of water along the creek channel on the raw 1 m lidar bed, with its edges at 19 water depths; drawn with modeled WSE m3-v2, or m4-v1 or m5-v1, which share its channel. Shown by default in the Creek Water Visualization.
description:
What this is
Water outlines for the creeks of the Jack and Laura Dangermond Preserve, California: one continuous ribbon of water along each creek channel, with its edges drawn for 19 water depths from 1 centimeter to 8 meters. Each outline vertex carries the creek-bed elevation (m NAVD88) as Z, so the water can sit at the right depth above the bed on a 3D map. Pair it with the inferred water surface elevations (m5-v1) to see where the water was at any hour. This is the version the Creek Water Visualization shows by default.

How it was made
At stations about 2 meters apart along the creek's lowest path in the 1-meter USGS 3DEP lidar, a cross-section is flooded to each depth and its two water edges are joined into a ribbon.

Accuracy and limits
These are estimates, not measurements. The stream flows are modeled without gauge correction and may be off by a factor of 2 to 5, so the timing of rises and falls is more reliable than the heights. The water depth assumes steady flow over a bare-earth lidar terrain that cannot see the underwater channel bed. Use them for research and visualization.

Service
https://dangermondpreserve-spatial.com/server/rest/services/Hosted/creek_water_visualization_wse_polygons_m3_v2/FeatureServer

Technical details

Dangermond Preserve — Creek Water Outlines (m3-v2, channel ribbon on the raw lidar bed, for m3-v2, m4-v1 and m5-v1). Data-Product Version m3-v2 of m3-flowline-channel-ribbon. Shared publicly as the Creek Water Visualization's default modeled water; other versions stay private.

How it is made: One continuous ribbon of water along the channel of each flowline, on the raw 1 m lidar bed at the creek’s lowest point of every station (no bed smoothing; road and railroad fills breached). At every station a 1-D cross-section flood gives the water edges for a ladder of depths; the edges are smoothed along the creek and kept monotone with depth. The browser smooths the water surface over ±5 × its depth and pool-fills it along the run (pools behind steps stand level, deep water drowns the bumps of the bed) and morphs between the depth rungs at each station’s own depth below that surface, so width changes continuously with time and neighbouring Creek Segments meet exactly. True water by default; ?ribbonDisplayFloorM=0.15&ribbonDisplayLiftM=0.3 turns on version 1’s steep-reach display exaggeration. The Time Series and the chart keep true values. Built on m3-v2. Built from modeled-wse m3-v2.

Change: implementation fix: Stage 4 flowline-channel-ribbon v2 built from modeled-wse m3-v2: version 2: built on m3-v2. Stations sit on the creek’s lowest point with the raw lidar (breached through tall short barriers) as ring z and the flood level; m3’s water-surface stations (shared with Stage 3); anchor at the lowest point with anchorStation, downstreamSegmentId and stationDistancesM saved; drawn pool-filled (browserDrawing channel-ribbon-pool-filled, the water smoothed over ±5 × its depth first) with the display rule off by default

Built from: modeled WSE m3-v2 (m3-flowline-profile-manning-depth)

Bucket bounds: min_depth_m and max_depth_m are WATER DEPTHS in meters above the bed, half-open [min, max); they are not water-surface elevations. Stage 4's JSON calls them minWaterSurfaceElevationM / maxWaterSurfaceElevationM to keep the file shape.

Vertex Z: bed elevation at the vertex, m NAVD88 (North American Vertical Datum of 1988), 3 decimals

Drawing: channel-ribbon-pool-filled: per station, the water surface is the modeled flowing depth smoothed over ±5 × the depth along the station distances (channel_ribbons.station_distances_m) and pool-filled along the run; the edges are the rungs around each station's own depth below that surface (morphed between rungs), drawn at that surface.

Geometry: each bucket's one stored ring is the polygon's only ring, in its stored vertex order (left edge stations 0…n−1, then right edge n−1…0), closed by repeating the first vertex; not reoriented and not repaired, so a ring crossing itself at a folded rung stays as it is

Channel ribbons table: One row per Creek Segment that has a ribbon, from its polygon set's channelRibbon: station_count, length_m, the anchor point (the anchor station's lowest point) and its bed, anchor_station (index among the stations), downstream_segment_id (next segment of the run, null at its end), breached_station_count, and three JSON arrays: station_distances_m_json (distance of each station from the upstream boundary station, m) and true_top_width_at_anchor_m_json / display_top_width_at_anchor_m_json (one width per depth rung, m). Fields a ribbon version does not store are null.
